newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends weaker in steady trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends weaker in steady trading.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended weaker on Monday at C$1.3780 (US$0.7256) from this morning's open of C$1.3719 (US$0.7289) in steady trade, pressured by a drop in the price of gold and gold stocks, dealers said. * They said the currency would likely weaken further on Tuesday as gold pressures continued.
Gold was fixed in London at $318.75 an ounce on Monday, its lowest level in 12 years amid a debate over whether central banks should hang on to their large reserves of gold bullion.

Central banks in the Netherlands, Belgium and Switzerland also have sold off gold reserves in recent years and the U.S. Federal Reserve issued a paper suggesting central banks had no need to hold gold.
Traders said that reality outweighed gains in Asia after the Japanese government reported a larger than expected increase in the nation's trade surplus.
Although market players were expecting a large increase in Japan's trade surplus, the 129.3 percent jump from the same period in the previous year was a surprise and strengthened the move to the yen.
The Canadian dollar weakened to C$1.3777 (US$0.7258) before staging a late session rally to the C$1.3735 (US$0.7280) level.
"We had some Japanese banks come back in and buy some Canada (dollars) and then we saw some Canadians in there as well," Farrill said.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar dipped to 81.86 Japanese yen from Friday's 83.09 yen and climbed to 1.2717 German marks from Friday's 1.2754 marks.
